alternative_explanations: Any D=16 success may come entirely from the hand-designed self-loop feature and supervised label construction rather than learned difficulty estimation.
confounds: Operation accounting charges perceptron arithmetic explicitly while older controls count their declared graph operations, so absolute cross-candidate constants remain an instrumentation convention.
falsification_criteria: Treat the learned implementation as invalid if it fails D<=4 despite correctly separated frozen controls or if its recorded source audit fails.
Count the quality-cost claim against HYP-0004 if D=16 accuracy is below 0.95 or if the exact learned controller uses at least as many mean operations as exact fixed max.

outcome_policy.negative: Failure on trained depths or D=16 would reject this minimal learned halt implementation and reduce confidence in easy length extrapolation.
outcome_policy.null: Exact D=16 transfer without an operation advantage would show local rule generalization but no end-to-end efficiency benefit at this depth distribution.
outcome_policy.positive: Exact D=16 transfer plus lower mean operations would support a learned local halting mechanism worth replicated screen testing.

predicted_outcome: The learned local halt rule should reach exact accuracy at D=1,4,16 with K slope near 0 and operation counts 10,25,85, giving mean 40 and depth slope near 0.77. It should therefore generalize the local decision to D=16 but be dominated in mean operations by exact fixed max at 16; adaptive indexed remains the mechanical oracle at mean 7.
promotion_criteria: Advance learned halting only if accuracy is 1.0 in every cell, K slope is near 0, D-dependent operations are below fixed max on average, and the candidate is on the accuracy-gated Pareto frontier; quick cannot promote the family.
research_question: Can a one-feature perceptron trained only on a terminal and at most four predecessor transitions preserve exact D=16 traversal without receiving D and remain cheaper than a fixed-depth solver after all halt-decision operations are charged?
title: Learned local halting with charged controller overhead
